rooms.8304: The great stone bridge ends here on a shelf of cracked grey rock, its last parapet stones tumbled and split as if some giant fist had struck them. South, the sundered span leaps back over the roaring gorge toward the Trade Road. A bleak, wind-scoured waste opens out on either hand, the badlands running away east and west under a low iron sky. Northward the ground lifts toward the dark, bare shoulders of the Black Hills.
rooms.8305: The first slopes of the Black Hills begin here, low and stony, the soil between them dark as soot and grown with nothing but wiry grass. A cold wind pours down from the heights and flattens the grass in grey ripples. The hills climb north and spread east and west in dull, rounded humps, while south the land falls back toward the sundered bridge. Somewhere far off, a crow calls once and is silent.
rooms.8306: Black shale crunches underfoot on this barren rise, splintered into thin plates that slide and clatter at every step. From the crest the gorge behind you shows as a dark scar across the land, and the Spirit Wood as a smudge of shadow far ahead. Hills roll on north, east and west, and the slope runs south down toward the bridge country. Nothing grows here but a crust of grey lichen.
rooms.8307: A tall cairn of black stones crowns this hilltop, half-collapsed, its builders long forgotten. The wind keens through the gaps between the stones with a thin, hollow note that sets your teeth on edge. A sheep track drops away west along the ridge and another runs east across the saddle, while the way you came falls south down the shale. Clouds the colour of wet slate hang low overhead.
rooms.8308: The hillside here is scarred by an old landslip, a raw bank of black earth and boulders that slid down long ago and never healed. Thorny gorse has taken hold among the stones, its few yellow flowers the only colour for miles. Paths wind north up the slope and east along the foot of the slip, while west and south they drop into the hollows between the hills. The air smells of cold stone and rain.
rooms.8309: A narrow gully cuts through the hill, its sides streaked black and rust-red where water has leached the iron from the rock. Pools of brackish water stand in the bottom, skinned with an oily film. The gully climbs north toward higher ground and opens south onto the lower slopes, and a goat path scrambles out of it to the east. Old bleached bones of some small beast lie wedged among the stones.
rooms.8310: This is one of the highest of the Black Hills, a bald, windswept dome where the grass has given up and left only bare dark rock. The wind never rests up here, and it pushes at you like an unfriendly hand. Far ahead a grey line of trees marks the edge of the Spirit Wood, and beside it rises a lone hill crowned by a single gaunt shape. The way runs east along the crown and south down into the gully.
rooms.8311: Several paths meet in a stony hollow between the hills, where a boundary stone leans at a drunken angle, its carvings worn smooth. North, a steeper path climbs toward a lonely hilltop where a gallows stands stark against the clouds. The other ways wander east and west along the folds of the hills, and south down a scree slope. The ground is trampled and muddy, as if many feet pass this way, though none linger.
rooms.8312: An old gallows of black, weather-split timber crowns this bleak hilltop, its crossbeam still bearing a frayed length of rope that turns slowly in the wind. The grass around its foot grows thin and pale, and no bird will settle on the beam. North, the hill falls away to the dark fringe of the Spirit Wood, and south a path drops back into the Black Hills. Even by day the air here feels cold and watchful.
rooms.8313: Here the open hills give way to the first trees of the Spirit Wood, grey and crooked, their bark peeling like dead skin. A chill mist lingers among the trunks even at midday, and the light turns thin and colourless. The wood thickens to the north, while to the south the hill of the gallows rises bare and dark. A deep hush lies over everything, as though the trees are holding their breath.
rooms.8314: The path winds between ancient yews whose branches knit together overhead into a low, black roof. Pale fungus glimmers on the rotting stumps, giving off a faint and sickly glow. Now and then a cold breath of air passes through the trees with no wind to carry it. The trail continues north deeper into the wood and south toward its edge.
rooms.8315: Grey moss hangs in long beards from the branches here, stirring gently though the air is still. The ground is soft and spongy, layered with years of fallen needles that swallow the sound of your steps. Faint whispers seem to drift between the trunks, always just too quiet to make out. The path leads north and south through the gloom.
rooms.8316: A ring of pale standing stones, none taller than your knee, encircles a patch of bare earth beside the path. Nothing grows inside the ring, and frost clings there even when the rest of the wood is merely damp. The trees press close around it, gnarled and leaning inward. The trail runs north between the trunks and south back toward the edge of the wood.
rooms.8317: Four paths meet beneath a dead oak, a vast and leafless giant whose branches spread like grasping fingers over the crossing. Strips of faded cloth are tied to its lowest boughs, prayers or warnings from travellers long gone. Paths lead off north, east and west into the wood, and south back toward the hills. The mist gathers thickest here, curling around the roots.
rooms.8319: The path ends in a hollow where the roots of two great trees have heaved the earth apart, laying bare a square stone hatch set in the ground. The hatch is bound with rusted iron bands and chained fast, shutting off the dark tunnel that leads down beneath it. Cold air seeps up through the cracks around its edges, smelling of damp stone and something older. The only open way is back south to the crossing.
rooms.8320: Ferns as tall as a man crowd the path here, their fronds grey with mist and dripping with cold water. Somewhere among them a brook trickles unseen. The way bends at this spot, running north toward a lighter patch in the trees and west back to the dead oak at the crossing. Webs hang thick between the ferns, beaded with droplets like strings of tiny pearls.
rooms.8321: The trees draw back to leave a round clearing open to a grey and cheerless sky, carpeted with pale, wiry grass. A blackened ring of fire-stones sits at its centre, cold and long unused. Paths leave the clearing on every side: north deeper into the wood, east toward the gleam of a small pond, west toward an old camp, and south back among the ferns. The silence here feels heavier than among the trees.
rooms.8322: The trees grow huge and close here, their trunks black with damp and their roots coiling over the ground like sleeping serpents. Very little light reaches the forest floor, and what does is grey and cold. Faint trails wind north and east into deeper shadow, west toward a great fallen trunk, and south back to the clearing. A low moaning seems to rise and fall among the branches, though no wind blows.
rooms.8325: The trail dies away among roots and brambles in a dead-end hollow where the trees stand so close that their trunks form a wall. Hundreds of small bones have been woven into the brambles, and they click faintly together whenever the mist stirs. The cold here bites through cloth and skin alike, and your breath smokes in the gloom. The only way out is back south through the dark trees.
rooms.8327: A sluggish black stream creeps through the roots here, so still and dark that it mirrors the branches above like a sheet of polished jet. Its banks are crusted with pale fungus that crumbles at a touch. A path follows the water east, another climbs north over a rise of roots, and a third leads west into the shadowed heart of the wood. The smell of rot hangs thick in the damp air.
rooms.8332: The trees thin a little here, and grey light filters down through a ragged gap in the canopy. Thistles and nettles grow rank along the path, their leaves furred with mildew. A crooked wooden post stands at the bend, its carved pointer long since rotted away. The path turns east along a low bank and south back down into the deep wood.
rooms.8333: Birches begin to appear among the darker trees, their white trunks scarred with black marks like closed eyes. The mist is thinner here, and the air smells faintly of open ground. North, daylight shows between the trunks where the wood comes to an end, and west the path winds back among the yews. A broken fence of split rails runs a little way beside the trail, then gives up.
rooms.8334: The Spirit Wood ends abruptly at a low bank, and beyond it a wide, grey grassland stretches north beneath an enormous sky. Wind sweeps across the open ground, bringing the smell of dust and dry grass. Behind you the trees stand in a dark, silent wall, the path vanishing south into their shadow. A weathered stake topped with an animal skull marks the place where the trail leaves the wood.
rooms.8338: Flat, dun-coloured grassland runs away on every side, broken only by clumps of thornbush and the odd grey boulder. The grass is short and brittle, cropped close by wind and beasts. Faint tracks lead north, east and west across the plains, and south the ground slopes gently down toward the edge of the Spirit Wood. The sky is huge and colourless, pressing down on the land like a lid.
rooms.9122: A dry watercourse wanders across the plain here, its bed nothing but cracked mud and rounded pebbles. Thistles nod along its banks in the endless wind. Open grassland stretches away north and east, west and south, without a tree or a roof in sight. Far off, a line of jagged peaks rises dim and blue beyond the grass.
rooms.9123: The ground hardens here, the grass growing in thin tufts between patches of bare, frost-split earth. A bitter chill creeps down from the north, where a great white shape like a crooked claw rises from the plain. Tracks run east and west across the grass, and south back toward the dry watercourse. Hoarfrost lingers in the hollows long after dawn.
rooms.9124: A huge outcrop of rock juts from the plain here, curved like a talon and sheathed in blue-white ice that never seems to melt. Freezing air flows down from it in a slow, invisible river, and the grass around its foot is stiff and white with rime. East, a rope bridge sways across a narrow ravine, while west and south the frozen plain opens out again. The ice creaks and groans faintly, as if the claw were flexing.
rooms.9129: A flimsy bridge of fraying rope and warped planks sways across a deep, narrow ravine, creaking with every gust. Through the gaps between the boards you can see the stony floor of the gorge far below, and the drop tugs at your stomach. The bridge leads east to an old gravel road and back west to the icy claw, while a trampled path follows the near rim of the ravine south. Several planks are missing altogether.
rooms.9168: An old road of packed grey gravel begins at the end of the rope bridge and strikes out east across a flat, lifeless plain. Its edges are lined with half-buried kerbstones, cut long ago by careful hands. Westward the rope bridge creaks over the ravine. Nothing grows beside the road but a few dead stalks rattling in the wind.
rooms.9169: The desolated plains stretch flat and featureless on both sides of the road, a waste of grey dust and cracked clay without a single blade of grass. The wind lifts the dust in slow, twisting columns that wander across the land and fall apart. The gravel road runs straight as a spear east and west. Your footsteps crunch loudly in the vast silence.
rooms.9170: A milestone stands beside the road here, a squat pillar of granite whose carvings have been scoured away by grit until only a faint pointing hand remains. Around it the plain is strewn with white stones like scattered teeth. The road goes on east toward distant hills and west toward the ravine. The sun, when it shows at all, is a pale coin behind the haze.
rooms.9171: The remains of a wagon lie in the ditch beside the road, its wheels broken and its timbers bleached silver by sun and wind. Whatever it once carried was taken long ago. Ahead the road begins to curve east toward rising ground, and behind you it runs back west across the empty plain. Dust has drifted in a soft grey bank against the wreck's side.
rooms.9172: The gravel road bends sharply here, turning north toward the foothills where the ground starts to buckle and climb. Banks of loose scree spill onto the road from a low cut in the land. Westward it runs back across the desolated plains toward the rope bridge. A cold wind smelling of snow comes down from the heights.
rooms.9173: The road reaches the foot of a steep slope and climbs it by rough steps cut into the rock, each one worn into a shallow bowl. The way up leads to a higher stretch of road along the hillside. South, the road runs back to its bend at the edge of the plains. Hardy thornbushes cling to the bank, their branches hung with tufts of grey wool.
rooms.9174: The road runs along a shelf cut into the hillside, with a sheer drop on one hand and a wall of crumbling rock on the other. Below, the rough steps lead down toward the plains, which spread away grey and endless beyond the foothills. North, the road continues along the shelf, climbing gently. Loose stones skitter away under your feet and vanish over the edge.
rooms.9175: The shelf widens into a level stretch of road, paved here with big flat slabs where the gravel has washed away. Old wheel ruts are worn deep into the stone, filled now with rainwater and dead leaves. The road turns east toward a dark tower that rises on a spur above the hills, and back south along the hillside. The wind has an edge of ice to it now.
rooms.9176: The road ends below a rocky spur, and a steep track zigzags up toward the grim old watchtower that crowns it. The tower's walls are dark with age, and the empty slits of its windows gaze down at you. West, the paved road runs back along the hillside. Thorn and bramble choke the foot of the slope, leaving only the narrow track clear.
rooms.9177: You stand on the windswept summit of the spur, at the foot of an old watchtower built of rough black stone. Its doorway gapes open to the east, the door long gone, and arrow slits stare out over the land below. North, a narrow path leads into the mouth of a deep canyon between towering walls of red rock. The track drops back down toward the road beneath the spur.
rooms.9161: The path enters the Canyon of Khel-zaram between walls of banded red and ochre rock that rise sheer for hundreds of feet. Only a narrow strip of sky shows overhead, and the canyon floor lies in cold shadow. North, the gorge winds on between the cliffs, and south the path climbs back out to the watchtower. Your voice comes back from the walls in strange, broken echoes.
rooms.9162: Boulders the size of cottages have fallen from the cliffs and lie jumbled across the canyon floor, leaving only a twisting path between them. Carvings of bearded faces, worn almost smooth, peer out from the rock walls at the height of a man. The canyon runs on north between the cliffs and back south toward its mouth. A thin trickle of water drips somewhere among the stones.
rooms.9163: The canyon ends against a towering wall of red rock streaked with white mineral stains, where a cold spring seeps from a crack and spreads across the floor. Here the path turns east, following the water out through a gap into a hidden valley. South, the canyon winds back between its cliffs. The air is damp and cool, and moss grows thick wherever the water runs.
rooms.9164: A small, deep valley opens among the mountains, its floor laced with a dozen shallow streams that wander and braid through beds of grey shingle. Mist hangs low over the water, and the light here is soft and dim even at noon. North, the streams gather toward the shore of a still mountain lake, while west a gap in the rock leads back into the canyon. The murmur of running water fills the vale.
rooms.9165: The dark waters of Lake Zaram lie still and cold beneath the peaks, so clear that pale stones show far beneath the surface. A narrow beach of black pebbles curves along the shore, crunching underfoot. West, a flight of rough steps disappears into a cleft in the mountainside, and south the shore leads back down into the vale of streams. No ripple stirs the water, and nothing rises to break it.
rooms.9166: A stair of rough-hewn steps enters the mountain through a tunnel barely wider than your shoulders. What little light there is filters in from the lake shore to the east, fading to a dim grey glow on the damp walls. The steps go on north into deeper darkness. Water drips steadily from the ceiling, and each drop echoes like a footstep.
rooms.9167: The dim stairs wind on through the heart of the rock, the steps slick with icy water and worn smooth by countless feet. Iron rings are set into the wall at intervals, rusted into lumps, where torches may once have burned. A breath of freezing air comes down from the north, where the stair rises toward the open mountainside. South, the steps descend toward the lake.
rooms.9156: The tunnel stair opens onto a trail along a bare mountainside, deep in old snow and glazed with ice. The wind howls across the slope, flinging needles of frost into your face. The trail climbs north along the mountain, and south it ducks back into the dim stairs. Far below, the lake lies like a dark mirror among the peaks.
rooms.9157: The frozen trail edges along a ledge where the snow has been packed into treacherous ice. Icicles as long as spears hang from the overhanging rock, dripping in the rare moments of sun. North the trail continues to climb, and south it winds back toward the stair. Every step must be tested before you trust your weight to it.
rooms.9158: The trail comes to the foot of an icy slope too steep to walk, where steps have been cut into the frozen snow and a frayed rope is pegged alongside them. The way up climbs toward a high shoulder of the mountain. South, the trail runs back along the ledge. The cold here is fierce enough to make your fingers ache inside your gloves.
rooms.9159: Atop the icy slope the trail levels out onto a broad shoulder of the mountain, swept nearly bare by a fierce, unending wind. East, a road of carved flagstones leads toward a great doorway set in the mountain's flank. The cut steps lead down the slope behind you. Rime feathers every rock, glittering in the thin light.
rooms.9160: Two immense doors of dark iron and stone are set into the mountainside here, carved with rows of bearded kings and bound with bands of tarnished bronze. This is Durgar's Gate, the way into the dwarven kingdom, and its doors lead north into the mountain, though they stand shut and barred, their great hinges locked with ice. Runes run around the arch above in a deep-cut band. West, the frozen trail leads back along the shoulder of the mountain.
rooms.9178: The inside of the watchtower is a single round chamber, its stone floor littered with fallen plaster and old bird droppings. A cold hearth is built into one wall, black with soot, and a broken table leans against another. Narrow stairs spiral up inside the wall toward the look-out above. West, the empty doorway lets in a grey square of daylight and a whistle of wind.
rooms.9179: The topmost chamber of the tower is a cramped room ringed by tall window slits, through which the wind moans and whistles. From here the watchers of old could see the plains far below, the dark line of the canyon, and the road snaking off across the waste. Names and dates have been scratched into the stone sills by long-dead sentries. A narrow stair leads down into the chamber beneath.
rooms.9128: The plain runs up to the edge of a narrow ravine here, a deep crack in the earth whose far side lies only a stone's throw away. North, a rope bridge sways over the gap. Tracks run south across the grass and west toward the open plain. Tough little shrubs cling to the ravine's lip, bent flat by the wind.
rooms.9127: Grey grass ripples away under the wind, and stones lie half-sunk in the earth like the backs of drowned beasts. Animal trails wander through the grass, north toward the ravine and south across the open ground. A wider track leads west toward the middle of the plains. The sky is empty and grey, without even a bird to break it.
rooms.9126: This corner of the plains is a shallow basin where rainwater collects in muddy pools and the grass grows longer and greener than elsewhere. The mud is crossed with paw prints and the sharp slots of hooves. A track leads north along the basin's rim, and west across the plain toward the trail from the Spirit Wood. Reeds rattle around the pools in the wind.
rooms.8339: The plains begin to rise here toward the mountains, the grass giving way to stony ground scattered with lichen-crusted rocks. North, a trail heads toward the mountain wall, a dark rampart of cliffs filling the horizon. East, the icy claw glitters coldly above the grass, while the open plain stretches south and west. The wind carries a faint smell of smoke from somewhere unseen.
rooms.8343: A stony trail climbs into the foothills, winding between boulders and stunted, wind-twisted pines. The plains spread out behind you, grey and endless, as the trail runs south back down to them. North it climbs on toward the cliffs. Loose rock clatters down from somewhere above, and the echoes take a long time to die.
rooms.8344: The trail turns sharply here around a great buttress of dark rock, its face scored with the marks of old tools. A cold spring trickles from the base of the cliff into a stone basin, cut long ago to catch the water. The trail continues east along the foot of the mountain and back south toward the plains. Moss grows thick and green around the basin, the only soft thing in sight.
rooms.8345: The trail ends against the sheer face of the mountain wall, a vast cliff of black rock that rises until it is lost in cloud. Iron pegs and worn handholds lead up the face, the only way onward. West, the trail runs back along the foot of the cliffs. Fallen stones litter the ground here, some of them stained dark.
rooms.8346: You cling to the mountain wall with the wind tearing at your clothes and nothing beneath your heels but empty air. Rusted iron pegs, hammered into the rock long ago, offer holds that creak alarmingly under your weight. The pegs lead up toward a ledge above and down to the trail at the cliff's foot. Far below, the plains lie spread out like a grey and faded map.
rooms.8347: A narrow landing juts from the cliff face, barely wide enough to stand on, its edge crumbling into the void. A dark crack opens in the rock to the east, just large enough to squeeze into. More pegs lead up toward the heights, where black shapes like columns stand against the clouds, and down the cliff toward the trail. Wind roars past the landing in sudden, buffeting gusts.
rooms.8356: This crevice is a tight crack in the mountain, its rough walls pressing in on both sides and its ceiling lost in blackness. The air is still and stale, and the only light comes from the landing to the west. North, the crevice narrows to a gap choked with fallen rock and closed by an old iron grille, beyond which some cave lies in darkness. Scratches in the stone near the grille look like the work of fingernails.
rooms.8348: Tall pillars of black basalt rise from a bare plateau here, dozens of them, standing in silent rows like an army of giants turned to stone. Their surfaces are glassy and cold, and nothing grows in their shadows. A mountain road leads away east between the last of the pillars, and west a dark opening leads into a winding trail inside the mountain. The pegs on the cliff lead down to a small landing below.
rooms.8349: A broad road of fitted stones runs across the high plateau, its paving cracked and heaved by frost. On either side the ground is bare grey rock, without soil or grass. North, the road climbs toward a gap between two peaks, and west it runs back among the black pillars. Somewhere ahead, the wind howls through a narrow place.
rooms.8350: The road climbs steadily between rising walls of rock, and the air grows thin and bitterly cold. Old cairns mark the way at intervals, each topped with a white stone. North, a deep chasm opens across the road ahead, and south the road leads back down toward the plateau. Snow lies in the cracks of the paving and in the lee of every boulder.
rooms.8353: The road ends at the brink of a terrible ravine, so deep that its bottom is lost in mist and shadow. Spanning it is a stone bridge no wider than a man's shoulders, without rail or wall, arching north over the abyss toward the far side. A weathered stone stands at the bridge's head, carved with a skull and a warning. South, the road leads back down between the peaks.
rooms.8354: You edge along the narrow stone bridge with nothing on either side but a sickening drop into mist and darkness. The wind shrieks up out of the ravine, snatching at you and trying to pull you off your feet. The far side lies north, and the bridge's head back south, both seeming impossibly far away. Small stones break from the span beneath your feet and fall without a sound.
rooms.8355: The narrow bridge comes to rest on a ledge of black rock at the far side of the ravine. A steep, crooked stair is cut into the cliff above, leading up toward a dark mass of walls and towers that loom against the clouds. South, the bridge stretches back over the abyss. The stones of the ledge are cold and slick with mist.
rooms.8357: A grim castle of black stone rises before you, its walls sheer and windowless, its towers lost in low, smoky cloud. The great gate stands to the south, a portcullis of iron bars rusted into place and shut fast, barring the way into the castle yard. Below the walls, the crooked stair leads down to the ledge above the ravine. No banner flies and no light shows, but the place does not feel empty.
rooms.9147: A trail winds through the inside of the mountain along a passage worn smooth by water and feet, its walls glistening black in the faint light. Daylight leaks in ahead, where the passage forks and both openings, north and east, come out among the dark pillars. South, the trail spirals back down into darkness. The air smells of wet stone and cold iron.
rooms.9146: The passage climbs in long, tight curves, the floor cut into shallow steps that are slick with seepage. The walls press close and the ceiling hangs low, forcing you to stoop in places. North, the trail winds on toward a faint grey light, and south it descends into an immense darkness. Your breathing sounds very loud in the narrow space.
rooms.9145: The passage opens onto the edge of a vast cavern whose floor stretches away flat and featureless into utter darkness, like a plain beneath a starless night. Somewhere high above, the unseen roof drips, and the drops fall a very long way. North, the winding trail begins its climb out of the cavern, and south a faint path marked by small stone cairns leads across the dark plains. The cold here is deep and still.
rooms.9144: Out on the dark plains the walls of the cavern have vanished altogether, and the darkness presses in on every side. The floor is fine black grit, crisscrossed with old footprints that lead nowhere in particular. The line of little cairns runs north toward the passage and south deeper into the cavern. A faint sound like distant breathing rises and falls in the blackness.
rooms.9143: The path across the dark plains ends at a shallow pit in the cavern floor, ringed with stones and filled with ancient ash and charred bones. The darkness is absolute beyond the reach of your light, and the silence feels like a held breath. The little cairns lead back north across the cavern toward the winding trail. A cold draught rises from the pit, carrying the smell of old smoke.
rooms.9133: Tufts of grey grass and low, spiny bushes cover the plain, and the earth between them is cracked into a pattern of dry plates. A ruined shepherd's hut of piled stones stands roofless here, its doorway facing the wind. Tracks lead north toward the foothills, east across the plain, south over the grass and west toward a dark line of trees. Tattered strips of hide flap from a pole beside the hut.
rooms.9132: The plains here are scarred by a wide burn, the grass reduced to black stubble and the earth crusted with ash. The smell of old smoke still clings to the ground. Grassland stretches unburned to the north and east, south and west, around the edges of the black patch. Charred bones of some large beast lie at the heart of the burn.
rooms.9125: A low mound rises from the plain here, covered with coarse grass and crowned with a ring of upright stones. From its top you can see the dark mass of the Spirit Wood against the grey land. The plain runs north and west from the mound, and east toward the path from the wood. Burrows have been dug deep into the mound's flanks, each ringed with a fan of pale spoil.
rooms.9130: This is the edge of the open plains, where the grass grows waist-high and grey and hisses ceaselessly in the wind. Hidden hollows and old pits make every step uncertain. Paths have been beaten through the grass north and east. Beyond the grass the land rolls away, empty and grey, to a horizon smudged with dust.
rooms.9131: The grass thins here into a stretch of hard-packed earth trampled by many feet, and the ashes of a recent fire lie in a blackened circle. Shards of broken pots and gnawed bones are trodden into the dirt around it. North, scrubby trees mark the start of a thicket; tracks lead east and south across the grass, and west toward a barricade on the horizon. The place stinks of smoke and of something rank and animal.
rooms.8341: Stunted thorn trees crowd together here in a thicket that has crept out across the plains, their branches black and knotted. The ground beneath them is bare and littered with dead thorns. Narrow ways wind through the thicket north and west, and out onto the open grass east and south. The trees creak and rattle in the wind like old bones.
rooms.8340: Deep in the thorn thicket the light turns dim and grey, and the branches knit overhead into a prickly roof. Tufts of coarse fur hang caught on the thorns at the height of a man's waist. A path through the thicket leads east back toward open ground, west deeper among the thorns, and south along a beaten track. A sour animal smell hangs in the still air.
rooms.8342: The thicket grows densest here, the thorn trees so tangled that they form a living wall. A hollow has been hacked into their midst, roofed with cut branches and floored with trampled earth. Ways lead east through the thorns and south toward the edge of the plains. The branches have been scratched with crude marks like claws or tally strokes.
rooms.9135: The thorn thicket gives way here to open grassland that slopes gently down toward a wide hollow. Wind-blown seeds drift through the air like grey snow. North, the thorns close in again; east, a path skirts the thicket's edge; and south, the grass runs on toward a palisade of stakes. Hoofprints and broad, clawed footprints are pressed together in the soft ground.
rooms.9134: The plains end here against a crude barricade of sharpened stakes and heaped thornbrush that runs across the land as far as you can see. Beyond it, to the west, rises the smoke of many fires, but the only gap in the barricade is blocked by a heavy timber gate lashed shut with rawhide. North and east, the grass stretches back across the open plains. Skulls of beasts and men are spiked along the tops of the stakes.
rooms.8329: A narrow track follows the bank of a dark stream through the trees, the water sliding past without a sound. Gnarled alders lean out over it, their roots trailing in the current like drowned hair. The track runs east toward a faint smell of woodsmoke, and west back toward the heart of the wood. Pale lights seem to drift above the water, vanishing whenever you look straight at them.
rooms.8330: The trees here bear old axe-marks, and many have been felled, leaving a scattering of grey stumps among the living trunks. A cart track, deeply rutted and overgrown with moss, leads east toward a building half-hidden among the trees. West, the stream-side track winds back into deeper shadow. Rows of cut logs lie rotting where they were stacked long ago.
rooms.8331: A long, low lodge of dark logs stands in a small clearing here, its roof of mossy shingles sagging and its chimney leaning. The heavy wooden door to the east is shut, its iron latch red with rust. Antlers are nailed above the doorway, bleached white by the weather. West, the cart track leads back into the trees of the Spirit Wood.
rooms.8335: The lodge is one long room, dim and cold, with a great stone hearth at one end and heavy trestle tables along the walls. Animal pelts, stiff and moth-eaten, hang from the rafters among strings of long-dried herbs. A trapdoor in the floor opens on a ladder leading down into the cellar, and a back door stands in the east wall. West, the front door leads out to the clearing. Everything is coated in fine grey dust, as though no one has lived here for years.
rooms.8336: Behind the lodge lies a small yard, enclosed by the trees and choked with weeds. A woodpile has collapsed against the wall, and an old chopping block still holds a rusted axe-head driven deep into its grain. Beyond the yard the Spirit Wood presses close and dark, with no path leading into it. The lodge's back door, to the west, is the only way out.
rooms.8337: The cellar is a low, earth-walled room that smells of damp and old decay. Broken barrels and empty shelves line the walls, and a few shrivelled roots still hang from hooks in the beams. In one corner the floor has been dug up and roughly filled in again, the earth mounded like a grave. A ladder leads up through the trapdoor into the lodge above.
rooms.8326: A colossal tree has fallen across the forest floor here, tearing up a great wheel of roots and earth that stands taller than a house. Its trunk, furred with moss and riddled with holes, blocks the way beyond. The hollow beneath the roots draws the eye, a darkness deeper than the shadows around it. The only path leads back east toward the deeper wood.
rooms.8323: A small, still pond lies in a hollow among the trees, its water black and glassy and ringed with pale reeds. The reflections in it are strangely clear, showing the trees, the grey sky, and sometimes shapes that are not there when you look up. Mist curls across the surface in thin, slow wisps. A path leads back west to the clearing.
rooms.8324: An abandoned camp lies under the trees here: a ring of stones around cold ashes, a lean-to of rotting branches, and the frayed remains of a canvas awning. Whoever camped here left in a hurry, for a blackened iron tripod still stands over the dead fire. The ground is scattered with the prints of boots, all leading away. The clearing lies back to the east.
rooms.8318: The path ends at the edge of a sunken hollow full of tangled briars and dead bracken. In the middle of the hollow stands a lone stone cross, leaning and green with lichen, its arms broken. No birds sing here, and even the wind seems to avoid the place. The only way out is back east to the crossing beneath the dead oak.
rooms.9112: A long ridge of black rock runs along the top of the hills here like the spine of some buried beast. From its crest you can see a lonely gallows on a hilltop, and beyond it the grey sprawl of the Spirit Wood. The ridge path runs east and west, and a stony way drops south into a sheltered hollow. The wind moans through the cracks in the rock.
rooms.9111: The hills flatten out into a bleak upland of coarse grass and black, peaty pools. A tumbledown wall of dry stones runs across the moor, built by hands long gone and now good for nothing but shelter from the wind. Paths lead south across the upland and west toward a rocky ridge. The pools reflect a sky the colour of ashes.
rooms.9110: The upland here is cut by old peat diggings, square black pits half full of brown water. Abandoned turves lie stacked and crumbling beside them. Paths wander north and south across the moor, and west toward the higher hills. The smell of wet earth and peat smoke hangs over the place, though no fire burns.
rooms.9109: A lone, lightning-blasted thorn tree stands on the moor here, its trunk split in two and charred black. The wind has bent it until its branches all point the same way, like a hand warning you back. Paths lead north and south across the open ground, and west into a hollow between the hills. Old rooks' nests, long deserted, clot the dead branches.
rooms.9108: A shallow stream crosses the moor here over a bed of black stones, its water stained the colour of strong tea. Stepping stones, set long ago, lead across it, some of them now tilted or sunk. Paths run north and south along the stream, and west up a gentle rise. Tufts of bog cotton nod white along the banks.
rooms.9107: The moorland ends at the brink of a steep drop, where the land falls away into a deep, mist-filled ravine. Far across the gulf, the dim shapes of mountains rise in ragged ranks. Paths lead north along the edge and west back across the moor. The wind rising from the ravine is wet and cold and smells of distant snow.
rooms.9106: Four sheep-tracks meet here beside a crude shrine of stacked stones, daubed with faded ochre signs. A hollow in the shrine is crusted with old candle wax and green smears where coins once lay, offerings to whatever watches over these hills. Tracks lead north into the hills, east toward the edge of a ravine, west across the slopes, and south down toward the badlands. The wind tugs at a tattered rag tied to the topmost stone.
rooms.9118: This broad, grassy saddle between two hills is dotted with grey boulders, some of them split open by frost. Sheep have worn deep paths through the turf, though the flocks are long gone. Tracks lead north up into the higher hills, east and west along the saddle, and south toward a crossroads shrine. The grass here is short and springy, starred with tiny white flowers.
rooms.9115: A steep, rocky slope rises here, its face pocked with the dark mouths of small caves and burrows. Loose black scree slides underfoot, and the climbing is hard going. Paths cross the slope north and south, and run east and west around its shoulder. A faint, sour smell of animal dens drifts from the cave mouths.
rooms.9114: The hills crowd together here into a maze of narrow valleys and knobbly ridges, all of the same dark rock. A trickle of water runs down the middle of the valley floor, feeding a few ragged ferns. Ways lead off north toward a stony hollow, east and west along the valley, and south down a slope of scree. It would be easy to lose your way among these folds of land.
rooms.9113: A broad, flat-topped hill rises here, its summit strewn with the tumbled stones of some ancient wall. From the top you can follow the dark hills rolling away on every side, and see a gash where a ravine cuts across them. Paths lead north and south over the summit, west toward the valleys, and east toward a stone gatehouse. Thin, grey grass grows among the fallen stones.
rooms.24700: A squat gatehouse of dressed grey stone blocks the way east, built by dwarven hands into a cleft between two hills. Its heavy oaken door, bound with iron, stands shut, and the arch above it is carved with a hammer and an anvil. Paths wander off north, south and west across the dark hills. The stonework is old but sound, and not a single block has slipped out of line.
rooms.24701: Beyond the gatehouse a paved terrace ends at the brink of a vast ravine, and a bridge of carved stone leaps out across it toward the far mountains. A massive iron gate, bolted and chained, closes the bridge's head to the east, its bars as thick as a man's wrist. West, the door leads back through the gatehouse to the hills. Mist boils up out of the ravine, hiding its depths entirely.
rooms.9116: A small tarn lies cupped among the hills here, its black water rippling in the wind. Heather and bilberry grow thickly around its shores, and a few hardy rowans cling to the rocks. Paths circle the tarn north, south, east and west, linking the hollows of the hills. The water is so dark that it seems bottomless.
rooms.9117: A long, gentle slope of rough pasture runs down the hillside here, crossed by the remains of an old field wall. Thistles and docks have taken over the pasture, and the wall's stones lie scattered where they fell. Paths lead north up toward a tarn, east across the slope, and west toward a grassy saddle. A rusted iron gate hangs from a single post in the wall, opening onto nothing.
rooms.9119: A flat shelf of land lies between the hills here, covered with coarse grass and sprinkled with black flints. Ruined sheepfolds stand at intervals, their walls fallen into low rings of stone. Paths lead north into the steeper hills, east across the shelf, south toward the lower slopes and west up a shale rise. Wind hums through the grass with a low, steady sound.
rooms.9105: The lower slopes of the Black Hills are scarred here by gullies where the rain has torn the thin soil away from the dark rock. Bare stones jut up through the turf like old broken teeth. Ways climb north into the hills, run east and west along the slopes, and fall south toward the badlands. The land is quiet but for the wind and the trickle of hidden water.
rooms.9100: The badlands stretch out bare and cracked here, a wasteland of grey clay furrowed by countless dry gullies. A few dead shrubs cling on in the shelter of the ridges. Westward lies the end of the sundered bridge, eastward the waste continues, and north the ground rises toward the Black Hills. The ground is so dry that every step raises a puff of fine dust.
rooms.9101: Strange towers of eroded clay rise from the badlands here, sculpted by wind and rain into fantastic shapes like melted candles. Between them the ground is a maze of narrow gullies. The way leads north toward the hills and west across the waste. The wind whistles through the clay towers with an eerie, mournful sound.
rooms.9121: The hills give way here to a high, windy field of thin grass edged with stones. A fallen standing stone lies half-buried in the turf, its face carved with spirals that the weather has nearly erased. Paths lead east toward a cairn-topped hill and south along the hillside. Far away, the land drops toward a broad, grey valley.
rooms.9120: A rough track runs along the hillside here, worn into the soil by generations of drovers and their herds. A wooden post leans by the way, notched with old marks that once told the distance to somewhere. The track runs north and south along the hill, and a path climbs east to the shale-strewn heights. Black feathers lie scattered in the grass around the post.
rooms.9104: The hillside here is cut into rough terraces, perhaps fields once, now gone to coarse grass and bramble. Low walls of stacked stones hold up the terraces, bulging and slipping under the weight of earth. Paths lead north along the hillside, east toward the first slopes of the hills, and south down to the badlands. The air is heavy with the smell of rain.
rooms.9102: The badlands are at their bleakest here, a plain of cracked grey clay where nothing grows at all. The cracks are wide enough to swallow a foot, and the ground rings hollow underfoot. East lies the end of the sundered bridge and west the waste runs on, while north the ground rises toward the hills. The sky hangs low and grey, threatening a rain that never comes.
rooms.9103: The badlands end here at the brink of the great gorge, a sheer drop into a roaring chasm where the river runs far below. There is no way down, and the far side is a distant wall of rock. The only path leads back east across the cracked clay. Spray from the river rises on the wind, leaving a fine wet sheen on the rocks.
rooms.8665: A small rocky path drops away from the King's Road, winding down a steep, wooded hillside between grey boulders furred with moss. Oak and hazel lean over the path, and their roots make rough steps in the stony soil. The way up climbs back to the road, and south the path descends deeper into the hills of the King's Forest. Somewhere below, water chuckles over stones.
rooms.8666: The path squeezes between two great slabs of grey rock that lean together overhead like the roof of a house. Ferns sprout from every crack, and the stone is cool and damp to the touch. North the path climbs toward the road, and south it winds on down the hillside. The air here smells of moss and old leaves.
rooms.8667: The trees open a little, and the path crosses a sloping meadow of bracken and foxgloves, bright against the dark woods around. A weathered stump has been carved into a rough seat, polished smooth by years of weary travellers. The path continues south down the slope and north back into the rocks. Sunlight falls warm and still across the bracken.
rooms.8668: The path runs along the foot of a low cliff here, where water seeps from the rock and drips into a chain of small pools. Hart's-tongue ferns and liverworts grow lush and green in the damp. North the path climbs back across the bracken slope, and south it bends toward a dark opening in the hillside. The quiet is broken only by the steady drip of water.
rooms.8669: The rocky path ends before the mouth of a cave in the hillside, a dark arch half-curtained by trailing ivy. Cold air breathes out from within, smelling of earth and wet stone. The cave opens to the south, while north the path climbs back up the hill. Scratches and old soot marks on the rock show that others have sheltered here before.
rooms.8670: The cave is a low, dry chamber hollowed into the hillside, its rough walls glittering faintly with flecks of quartz. A ring of blackened stones on the floor marks an old fire, and a shelf of rock along one wall makes a rough bed. Daylight filters in through the ivy at the entrance to the north. The air is still and smells of old smoke and damp earth.
rooms.8694: A narrow gap opens into a hidden hollow beneath the roots of a great tree, roofed with tangled roots and packed earth. Someone has made a den of it, with a bed of dried bracken, a few pegs driven into the roots for hanging things, and a small pit for a fire. Pale light filters down through the roots from somewhere above. North, the passage leads back to the bottom of the well.
rooms.8695: You stand at the bottom of an old dry well, a shaft of mossy stones rising to a ring of daylight high above. Iron rungs set into the wall lead up toward the ruins of the city overhead. The floor is soft with fallen leaves and old mud, and ferns grow from the cracks in the stonework. South, a low gap in the well's side opens into a hidden passage among the roots.
rooms.8742: Mossy steps lead down from the small island into a sunken hollow where a great barrow mound rises, grassed over and ringed by leaning stones. A doorway of massive stone slabs is set into its side beneath a carved lintel, but a fallen block seals the darkness beyond. The way up leads back to the trees of the small island. The air here is unnaturally still, and even the birds fall silent.
rooms.8745: A broad ledge of grey stone juts from the steep slope here, a natural balcony above a sea of treetops. Beyond its edge the King's Forest spreads away into the haze, its hills rolling and wooded. A goat track zigzags up the slope behind you toward the animal path. Lichen in rusty orange patches crusts the rock, and the wind smells of pine resin.
rooms.8746: This is a deep hollow beneath an overhanging bank, where a great badger sett has been dug into the soft, sandy earth. Heaps of excavated soil and old bedding lie before the dark entrances, and the smell of musk is strong. Roots dangle from the bank, and a steep scramble leads up to the trail. The ground is pocked with pawprints and scored by sharp claws.

8307.description: The cairn was once taller than a man, built of flat black stones fitted without mortar. A hollow at its heart, now open to the weather, holds nothing but wind-blown grit and a few green copper stains.

8312.description: The gallows is old enough that its uprights have split from top to bottom, yet it still stands. The rope on the crossbeam ends in a noose worn smooth and dark, and it sways even on the stillest days.

8316.description: Each stone is cut with a single shallow mark, a hand with fingers spread, worn almost away. Touching one leaves your fingers numb with cold for a long while after.

9124.description: Deep inside the ice, blurred as if seen through cloudy glass, dark shapes hang frozen: twisted roots, a broken spear, and something that might once have been a hand. Your own breath frosts the ice when you lean close.

9170.description: Only the carved hand survives, its finger pointing along the road toward the hills. Someone has scratched a tally of short lines beneath it, dozens of them, as if counting days or the dead.

9162.description: The faces are dwarven, broad and solemn, with braided beards that fall into knotwork borders. Each wears a different crown, and each has had its eyes chiselled out by some later, angrier hand.

9160.description: The runes are dwarven and cut as deep as a finger. Those who can read them make out a name, Durgar, and a warning that the mountain keeps what it is given.

9179.description: Dozens of names crowd the sills, some neat, some little more than scratches. The last one, cut deeper than the rest, is followed by a single word: alone.

8348.description: Each pillar has six flat sides, as if cut by a mason, though no tool could have shaped so many. Close up, faint reflections move in their glassy surfaces a moment after you do.

8353.description: Beneath the carved skull, letters in an old hand read: ONE AT A TIME, AND DO NOT LOOK DOWN. Someone has added a long list of names below, each crossed through.

8337.description: The earth is loose and dark, as if it was turned not so long ago. A wooden spoon has been pushed upright into the top of the mound, like a marker, and the cold that rises from it is far deeper than the cellar's.

8318.description: Beneath the lichen, letters run down the shaft of the cross: HERE LIES THE KEEPER OF THE LODGE, WHO WOULD NOT LEAVE. The stone is always cold and faintly wet to the touch.

24700.description: The hammer and anvil are cut in the crisp, deep style of dwarven masons, and beneath them a line of runes names the gatehouse as the Ravine Ward of Aredrel. The door's iron studs are each shaped like a tiny bearded face.

9121.description: The spirals wind inward to a small hollow at the stone's heart, worn smooth as if by countless thumbs. Rainwater gathers there and never quite seems to dry.

8742.description: The lintel is carved with a line of armed figures walking hand in hand into a door of knotwork. The last figure has been chipped away, as if someone wished to unmake him.

creatures.long_desc: A carrion crow hops along the ground, picking at something you would rather not see.
creatures.description: A big, ragged black crow with a heavy grey beak and dull, knowing eyes. Its feathers are matted with dust, and it keeps its head cocked toward you as though weighing how long you might last out here.

creatures.long_desc: A lean badland jackal slinks between the rocks, lips curled back from yellow teeth.
creatures.description: It is a gaunt, sandy-grey dog with oversized ears and ribs that show plainly through its mangy coat. It moves in a low, sidelong trot and never quite turns its back on you, and its yellow eyes are bright with hunger.

creatures.long_desc: A gnoll raider prowls here, sniffing the wind and swinging a spiked flail.
creatures.description: A hulking, hyena-headed gnoll stands taller than a man, its spotted hide covered in scraps of stolen leather and rusted mail. Its muzzle is scarred and grinning, and it gives off a rank stink of carrion and smoke. A string of teeth and finger-bones rattles at its neck.
rooms: The Old Gravel Road Crossing The Desolated Plains

creatures.long_desc: A hill troll squats among the rocks, gnawing on a thighbone.
creatures.description: The troll is a stooped mountain of grey-green flesh, its warty hide crusted with lichen and dirt. Its arms hang nearly to the ground and end in black, cracked claws, and its small eyes peer out from under a heavy brow with dull malice.

creatures.long_desc: A restless spirit drifts between the trees, its pale face twisted in sorrow.
creatures.description: It is the grey, half-transparent shape of a man or woman, its features blurred like a face seen through rain. Its mouth moves endlessly without a sound, and a bitter cold comes off it, frosting the leaves wherever it passes. A fine grey ash sifts from its hems as it moves.
rooms: The Southern Edge Of Spirit Wood

creatures.short_desc: the ghost of the hanged man
creatures.long_desc: The ghost of the hanged man sways beneath the gallows, a noose still tight about his neck.
creatures.description: He is a grey, gaunt shape in the rags of an old coat, his head bent at a dreadful angle by the rope that still hangs from his neck. His eyes are empty hollows, yet they follow you wherever you go. His lips are black, and when the wind drops you can hear him whispering the name of the man who hanged him.
rooms: The Hill Of The Hanged Man

creatures.long_desc: The ghost of the lodge-keeper shuffles about his old haunts, holding up a dim lantern.
creatures.description: A stooped old man in a leather apron and a woodsman's hood, all of him grey and faint as smoke. He lifts his lantern to peer at each visitor in turn, and his face crumples with anger when he finds a stranger. Earth clings to his hands and knees, as though he dug his own grave.

creatures.long_desc: A grey web spider the size of a dog clings to a tree trunk, its legs folded tight.
creatures.description: Its bloated grey body is furred with bristles and marked with a pale pattern like a skull. Eight black eyes glitter above a pair of dripping fangs, and threads of sticky silk trail from its spinnerets wherever it creeps. It has come out of the dark woods of Haon-Dor, or its mother did.

creatures.long_desc: A black-robed cultist stands here, chanting softly over a guttering black candle.
creatures.description: His robe is black wool stitched with a spider in silver thread, and his face is painted grey with ash. His hands are stained with wax and old blood, and he murmurs the same few words over and over in a tongue you do not know. He bears the mark of the dark temple of Haon-Dor on the back of one hand.

creatures.long_desc: A grizzled badger snuffles among the roots, digging for grubs.
creatures.description: A low, broad badger with a striped black-and-white face and a coat of coarse grey hair. It is short-tempered and strong, and its long front claws are caked with earth.

creatures.long_desc: A red fox pauses on the path, one forepaw raised, watching you with bright eyes.
creatures.description: A slim fox with a russet coat, black stockings and a bushy white-tipped tail. It is wary and quick, and its sharp face seems to wear a look of private amusement.

creatures.long_desc: A furtive poacher crouches in the shadows, a coil of wire snares over his shoulder.
creatures.description: A wiry, unshaven hunter in a patched green coat, smelling of woodsmoke and blood. A knife hangs at his belt and a bundle of snares at his shoulder, and his darting eyes say he has no wish to be found by the King's foresters or anyone else.

creatures.long_desc: A barrow wight stands guard before the mound, cold light burning in its eyes.
creatures.description: It is a tall, withered corpse in the corroded mail of an ancient chieftain, its skin drawn tight and grey over the bones. A pale light burns in its empty eye sockets, and rings glint on its skeletal fingers. The air around it is as cold as a winter grave.

items.room_desc: A crude spiked flail lies here, its chain caked with rust.
items.description: A knotted wooden haft is joined by a length of rusty chain to an iron ball hammered full of crude spikes. It is ugly, heavy and stained with old blood.

items.room_desc: A short loop of frayed rope, tied in a hangman's knot, lies here.
items.description: A hand's length of old, dark rope tied in a perfect hangman's knot, worn smooth by the grip of a dead man's neck. It is always cold, and some say it brings luck to anyone bold enough to carry it.

items.room_desc: An old iron lantern with horn panes sits here.
items.description: A sturdy iron lantern with panes of scraped horn, its handle wrapped in worn leather. Its flame burns low and steady and never seems to need trimming.

items.room_desc: A small pouch spilling fine grey ash lies here.
items.description: A twist of cloth holding a pinch of fine, cold grey ash that never quite settles. Hedge-witches and priests pay well for it.

items.room_desc: A skein of grey spider silk lies here, faintly sticky.
items.description: A tangle of grey silk as strong as wire and still a little sticky, wound into a rough skein. Weavers prize it for cloth that turns a blade.

items.room_desc: A swollen, glistening venom sac lies here.
items.description: A bulging sac of dark venom cut from a giant spider, its skin tough and shiny. Alchemists and assassins alike will pay for it, though it must be handled with great care.

items.room_desc: A thick black candle stands here, its wick charred.
items.description: A fat candle of black wax, carved with a spider and a ring of tiny, cramped letters. It burns with a smoky, greenish flame and smells of rot and myrrh.

items.room_desc: An ancient leaf-shaped sword lies here, green with age.
items.description: A broad, leaf-shaped sword of dark bronze, its hilt bound with gold wire and its blade etched with running hounds. It was laid in the barrow beside a forgotten king, and its edge is still keen.

items.room_desc: A coil of fine brass wire, knotted into a snare, lies here.
items.description: A running noose of fine brass wire on a wooden peg, the tool of a poacher's trade. A gamekeeper would pay a bounty to see it, and a poacher would pay more to have it back.

items.room_desc: A tarnished silver ring lies here.
items.description: A heavy silver ring blackened with age, set with a cloudy grey stone. Taken from a barrow-dweller's finger, it feels cold no matter how long it is worn, and quiet thoughts come easier with it on.
